We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some building blocks: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) available cheap (price 39.6 for 100g). Also we need the other aryl part: maybe an aniline with a cinnamoyl amide attached: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (a phenyl with para substituent of trans-cinnamoyl anilide). Could be built via sulfonamide coupling of sulfonyl chloride with an aniline that already has the cinnamoyl amide attached.

So step 1: Synthesize the aniline with cinnamoyl amide: 4-aminophenyl attached to trans-cinnamoyl amide? Actually the fragment is: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. That's a phenyl ring (para unsubstituted) bearing a trans-cinnamoyl amide substituent at para? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This is a phenyl ring with a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (an anilide with an aniline at the amide nitrogen). So the side chain is trans-cinnamoyl attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the side chain is: trans-cinnamoyl (CH=CH-CO-) attached to an aniline (NH-Ph-NH2). So the whole side chain is: -CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (where the phenyl is unsubstituted). So the whole fragment is a phenyl ring (the one attached to sulfonyl) bearing that side chain.

Thus we can think of building the side chain via amide formation between trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or acid) and 4-aminophenyl? Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para? Actually it's just an aniline). So we need 4-aminobenzaldehyde? No.

Simplify: target molecule = p-tolyl sulfonyl attached to para-aniline (the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the phenyl ring). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide is formed between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the phenyl ring with side chain). So step 1: sulfonylation.

Thus we need the aniline (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2) as a commercially available? Likely not. So we need to synthesize it in up to 2 steps.

Potential route: start from 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually we need a phenyl ring with a side chain at para position: trans-cinnamoyl anilide. Could be made by first forming the amide between trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) and 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl). That gives p-aminophenyl trans-cinnamamide (i.e., 4-aminophenyl attached to CO-CH=CH-). Then we need to have the aniline (NH2) on the amide nitrogen? Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is -CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that has an NH2 para? Actually the phenyl is c3ccccc3N meaning an aniline (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that has an NH2 substituent (maybe at para? Not specified). The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an NH2 at position 1 (attached to N) and another NH2 at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N is the amide N). The trailing N after the ring is an amine attached to the aromatic carbon (i.e., an aniline). So the phenyl has an NH2 substituent at the position where the amide attaches? Wait the SMILES: ...C(=O)N c3ccccc3 N. The N after the ring is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1). So the amide nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (i.e., the amide is attached to the phenyl at position 1). The trailing N is an aniline substituent on the same phenyl (maybe at para? Not indicated). Actually "c3ccccc3N" is an aniline (aniline). So the phenyl has an NH2 substituent at the position where the amide attaches? No, the amide attaches to the phenyl via the nitrogen (N attached to carbonyl). So the phenyl is attached to the amide nitrogen (i.e., N-aryl amide). The phenyl also has an NH2 substituent (aniline). So the phenyl is 4-aminophenyl? Could be para-aminophenyl (aniline). So the amide is N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide.

Thus the side chain is N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide.

Thus the aniline we need is 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl) which is commercially available (p-phenylenediamine). That's cheap.

So we can make N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide by reacting trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) with p-phenylenediamine (one amine reacts). Use protecting group maybe to protect the other amine, but we can use selective acylation of one amine (p-phenylenediamine) with trans-cinnamic acid chloride under conditions that favor monoacylation. Could also protect the other amine as Boc, then deprotect later.

Thus route:

Step A (retrosynthesis): target -> sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline fragment (N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide). So disconnection: break S-N bond.

Leaves: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide (needs synthesis).

Step B: N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide can be made by amide coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) with p-phenylenediamine, protecting the second amine (maybe as Boc) then deprotect.

Option 1: Use Boc-protected p-phenylenediamine (Boc-PDA) commercially? Could be "tert-butyl (4-aminophenyl)carbamate". That's available.

Search for "Boc-p-phenylenediamine".
